title: Indian Universities Nearly Quintuple Presence in QS World Rankings Since 2015 as IIT Delhi Hits Record 118th
excerpt: India now has 52 universities in the QS World Rankings, up from 11 a decade ago, with IIT Delhi achieving the highest position ever for an Indian institution.
body:
• India now has 52 universities in the QS World Rankings 2027, up from just 11 in 2015 — a nearly fivefold increase that makes it the fifth most represented country globally.
  • IIT Delhi topped Indian institutions at 118th globally, equalling the best-ever ranking by an Indian university. IIT Bombay dropped to 134th.
  • Of 52 ranked Indian universities, 26 improved their positions, 9 held steady, 15 declined, and 2 entered the rankings for the first time.
  • VIT recorded the sharpest jump among Indian institutions, climbing 94 spots to 597th, followed by BITS Pilani (up 93 to 575th).

India's Fastest Growth Among G20 Nations

India's footprint in global higher education rankings has expanded dramatically, with 52 universities now featured in the QS World University Rankings 2027 — up from just 14 in 2017, representing a 271% increase that stands as the fastest proportional growth among G20 nations, according to data released by QS Quacquarelli Symonds.

https://x.com/CataPaul2/status/2086422199246663742

The Indian government highlighted the broader trajectory: from 11 institutions in 2015 to 52 in 2027, nearly a fivefold increase. India now trails only the United States, United Kingdom, mainland China, and Germany in representation.

Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan said the results reflected the impact of reforms introduced under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020.

"India's strong performance in the latest global university rankings reflects the transformative impact of NEP 2020, with 52 universities across 19 states and union territories now represented and more than half improving their positions."

— Dharmendra Pradhan, Union Education Minister

IIT Delhi Equals India's Best-Ever Ranking

IIT Delhi retained its position as India's top-ranked university, climbing to 118th globally from 123rd the previous year. The ranking equals the highest position ever achieved by an Indian institution in the QS index, which was previously held by IIT Bombay at 129th in the 2026 edition.

IIT Bombay, meanwhile, slipped from 129th to 134th — continuing a two-year slide. IIT Madras was the only other Indian institution in the global top 200, improving to 170th from 180th.

How India's Top Institutions Performed

The IITs continued to dominate India's top 10. IIT Kharagpur held at 205th, IIT Kanpur at 221st, and the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) Bangalore at 221st. The University of Delhi improved to 322nd, IIT Roorkee to 335th, and IIT Guwahati held at 349th.

Among the biggest movers, VIT surged 94 positions to 597th, BITS Pilani climbed 93 spots to 575th, and IIT Hyderabad leaped 76 places to 588th. IIT BHU Varanasi rose 56 spots to 510th, while Shoolini University climbed 51 positions to break into India's top 10 at 452nd.

Jamia Millia Islamia recorded the largest jump among central universities, advancing 75 positions to 686th. The University of Delhi and JNU each improved by six places.

What the Rankings Measure

QS evaluates universities across indicators including academic reputation, faculty-student ratio, citations per faculty, employer reputation, internationalisation, sustainability, and employment outcomes. MIT retained the global top spot for the 15th consecutive year, followed by Stanford, Imperial College London, Oxford, and Harvard.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For Indian-origin families weighing higher education options, the rankings reflect a broader shift in how Indian institutions are perceived globally. The rise of private universities like VIT, BITS Pilani, and Shoolini alongside the traditional IIT-IISc hierarchy suggests a diversifying landscape. More than half of India's ranked universities improved their standing this year, a signal that the gains are broad-based rather than concentrated at the top.

Pradhan added that the progress underscored "the rise of a diverse, decentralised and globally competitive higher education system."
